english.title: Destroy or damage an ancient protected monument
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse destroyed or damaged a protected monument, namely **(..SPECIFY MONUMENT..), knowing that it was a protected monument and intending to destroy or damage the monument or being reckless as to whether the monument would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to section 28 of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
date and place

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: "Protected monument" means any scheduled monument and any monument under the ownership or guardianship of the Secretary of State or the Commission or a local authority by virtue of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
